A housing 'crisis'? Lets think about this.

The UK has free markets, remember. Why do the house prices keep going up? Because the banks keep bunging money at people to buy houses, rather than build them. It is very easy and profitable and risk free for them to lend money to buy an already existing house. They take on risk if the house doesn't exist yet and has to be constructed.

If you want an "affordable" house, try getting one away from London. Don't expect "affordability" in Mayfair. But there aren't any jobs out in the countryside, people moan. Well, if house prices there are a lot lower, companies could pay lower wages, as their staff wouldn't need such large mortgages. In time, they will relocate. Some are surely doing so already.

The 'crisis' might be more correctly called a bubble. We know what happens when there is a bubble for a particular commodity: it bursts. This would translate into a crash in real-estate prices. However, there are a lot of vested interests in not letting that happen. So what else will happen, instead?

I think that if the prices of houses won't drop, then there will be wage inflation, instead. Workers will require and begin to demand ever higher salaries, in order to bring their income into line with housing prices. Until inflation of wages alongside stagnation of housing prices restores a balance, people will have to commute great distances every day.

Why do people even want to buy houses? They sure wouldn't, if they thought that the price of the house was going to decline or stagnate. The market should correct itself. There is no need to fuel it.
